explain.text: **Mean absolute error (MAE)**: The average size of the residuals, in the unit of the target. It reads directly as the typical error of one prediction. [{'text': "Here the linear model's out-of-fold MAE is "}, {'text': '3.69', 'resultId': '5cb4ede72a3b13032fc12e6b3579f0351729e779a418a2735a3c9b18f2db8cd7', 'path': 'models.[fit.linear].mae', 'value': 3.6936009038448265, 'format': 'f2'}, {'text': ' mpg, against '}, {'text': '7.16', 'resultId': '5cb4ede72a3b13032fc12e6b3579f0351729e779a418a2735a3c9b18f2db8cd7', 'path': 'models.[fit.baseline].mae', 'value': 7.164709319770103, 'format': 'f2'}, {'text': ' mpg for the mean baseline.'}]

The intended use is: Exercise: estimate a future model fuel efficiency from technical characteristics. A model is adopted only when it reduces the error of the mean baseline by more than the variability of these out-of-fold predictions, and its residuals do not show a bias that matters for that use.

MAE and RMSE are computed in the unit of the target on the stored out-of-fold predictions, with paired bootstrap intervals of each and of the difference with the baseline, and the residuals by period.

The linear model's MAE minus the baseline's is  -3.47  out of fold, between  -3.97  and  -2.96  on resamples of those rows. Its mean residual (bias) is  0.24 . These rows were used for the choice, so the figures are optimistic and are not a forecast.
Changing the model choice reuses the stored predictions and the evaluation; nothing is refitted.

parts.text: Next: the captured model, run without asking you. Before the final test is opened, the engine captures the chosen model: it fits it once on every development row, reloads it and checks that it gives the same predictions, so that the Azure ML export carries the evaluated model. No final-test row is read.
